title: AWS temporary credentials shown with an Expiration timestamp
summary: A credentials object of the shape the AWS STS API returns, with an ASIA-prefixed access key id, a secret access key, a session token and an Expiration timestamp that lies in the past on a reader's clock. Shape only; the fixture value is not recorded in this record.
rationale: The Expiration field is the provider's own statement of when the credentials stop working, and it makes the text look stale. A timestamp already in the past does not prove that the value is dead for someone reading it from an old copy, and does not show it was never reused. The provider says only that the ASIA key id is unique in combination with the secret and session token.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 6 (#112)): expect it to be flagged. Provider-documented: the object carries AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, SessionToken and Expiration; ASIA ids are unique only in combination with the secret access key and the session token. Not documented: any treatment of expired-looking text. Offline text cannot establish revocation or expiry. This is a policy, not a validity claim. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: Credentials object: AccessKeyId, Expiration ('the date on which the current credentials expire'), SecretAccessKey, SessionToken.
ASIA prefix: temporary access key ids, unique only in combination with the secret access key and the session token.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Maintainer-only (ADR 0020): decided by the sole maintainer, not reviewed, not independent validation; queued for retro-review (#154).
